title: AT 2025abao (Bao): observed evidence, model inference and forecast for a stellar merger in M31
question: Which statements about AT 2025abao are direct observations, which are model-dependent inferences, and which are forecasts? Concretely: (1) What do the primary record (Karambelkar et al., Nature, DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-11221-z; arXiv:2611.23470) and the JWST Director's Discretionary Time observations (Program 12487, 2025-12-24) establish about the eruption, the ~7 solar-mass AGB primary, the ~0.7 solar-mass companion and the common-envelope history? (2) Which reported values are direct measurements, which are simulation-dependent reconstructions, and which are derived constraints such as the common-envelope efficiency? (3) What remains open or forecast-only, including the expected yield of similar transients from Roman time-domain surveys? Label each statement with an ecosystem reliability marker (R/T/H/S/OFFEN) and a provenance/verification level per ECO-ARC-0036, and record the TNS designation for AT 2025abao.
why_now: A 2026-11-19 evidence note drafted in kueper-ecosystem (docs/research/) is withdrawn because this repository must not carry domain content (README "Nicht-Zweck"; docs/repository-roles.md §2-§5). The underlying event was published in Nature on 2026-11-18, but the withdrawn note rested on secondary press coverage only; the primary record, the JWST program and the TNS designation must be pinned before KG/OTA/NOXIA consumers use any part of it. The non-canonical candidate belongs in kueper-knowledge-graph/research/candidates/ (ECO-ARC-0021 §2; research/policy.json candidate_path).

claim_class_scope.R: Observed multi-instrument detections, observation dates, publication facts and the TNS designation.
claim_class_scope.T: Model-dependent stellar parameters (~7 solar masses, ~350 solar radii, ~0.7 solar masses) and the reconstructed common-envelope history.
claim_class_scope.H: Falsifiable forecast of additional similar transients in Roman time-domain surveys; not established by this single event.
claim_class_scope.OFFEN: Post-merger state and a discovery rate for comparable transients.

observed_evidence.note: Detections and dates are reported observations; the Nature version was not directly retrievable, so the check rests on the arXiv record and secondary coverage.

inference_model.note: Masses and common-envelope history are reconstruction/simulation dependent, not direct measurements.

forecast.note: Roman yield forecast and post-merger state are not established by this event.

project_relevance.note: KUEPER-side consumer mapping; no claim about the event itself.

real_world_anchor: Transient AT 2025abao (TNS; reported 2025-10-20) in M31; JWST Director's Discretionary Time Program 12487 (PI: Karambelkar), MIRI observation 2025-12-24; Karambelkar et al., "An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion", Nature (published online 2026-11-18), DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-11221-z, arXiv:2611.23470.
